params.body:
## What

**Two tabs in the site settings.** "Pagina Stories" opens the brand's whole site settings document, so its first field was "Standaard SEO", with a title that has nothing to do with Stories. The document now has two tabs:

- **Stories**, with "Stories tonen" and the Stories page (video, intro, featured story), unfolded. It is the first tab, so "Pagina Stories" opens on it. It is hidden for a brand without Stories.
- **Algemeen**, with everything else. A brand without Stories opens here.

The "All fields" tab is hidden. Every field sits in one of the two tabs, and a test keeps it that way.

**Standaard SEO says what it is.** It is the brand's fallback, not the SEO of one page:
- the title is used only for a page without a title;
- the description is used for a page without its own description;
- the share image is used for a page without its own image.

The meta title gets the same check as the other titles: on hoet.be it warns to leave "Hoet" out. Today it holds "Hoet - Onopvallend opvallende brillen".

## Checked

- 98 tests pass (`vitest`, without the token-bound `config.test.ts`), with the new `tests/settings-groups.test.ts`.
- `tsc` and `sanity schema validate` (0 errors, 0 warnings) pass. Lint shows the same problems as on main, none in the changed file.
- The tab that opens first follows Sanity's rule: a group marked default, otherwise the first visible one.
- Not yet seen in a running Studio, which sits behind the login.

## After merge

`npm run deploy` for the Studio.
params.title: Split the site settings into a Stories and an Algemeen tab
